steps.title: Riesling
steps.body: Riesling is the most planted grape, about 25% of the Pfalz, one of the world's largest Riesling areas. The warm climate gives ripe peach, apricot and citrus, with fuller body and good acidity. Most is dry. The Mittelhaardt villages make some of Germany's greatest Rieslings.

steps.title: The Pinot family and others
steps.body: Spätburgunder, Pinot Noir, has grown fast in the south, alongside Weissburgunder, Pinot Blanc, and Grauburgunder, Pinot Gris. Dornfelder, a dark red cross, is popular for everyday wine. Müller-Thurgau, Silvaner, Scheurebe and Gewürztraminer also grow here. The Pfalz is Germany's most diverse region.

steps.prompt: Match each German name to its grape.
steps.explanation: The Pfalz grows a wide range of grapes.

steps.body: The Südpfalz, near Alsace, is a source of excellent Spätburgunder. Producers like Friedrich Becker grow vines right on the French border.

steps.prompt: Which is the Pfalz's most planted grape?
steps.explanation: Riesling, about a quarter of vineyards.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Riesling leads, ripe and mostly dry
The Pinot family is rising, especially in the south
